nodes.name: Stratification of Rep(G,R) via cohomological support
nodes.statement: One approach to such a classification for $\mathrm{Rep}(G,R)$ is based on cohomological support, which assigns to any representation a subset of the homogeneous Zariski spectrum of $H^*(G;R)$. Moreover, it descends to a map \[ \begin{Bmatrix} \text{Localizing tensor ideals of } \mathrm{Rep}(G,R) \end{Bmatrix} \xymatrix@C=2pc{ \ar[r]^-{} &} \begin{Bmatrix} \text{Subsets of } \mathrm{Spec}^h(H^*(G;R)) \end{Bmatrix}. \] We say that $\mathrm{Rep}(G,R)$ is \emph{stratified} if this map is a bijection.
nodes.statement_short: Rep(G,R) is stratified if cohomological support gives a bijection between localizing tensor ideals and subsets of Spec^h(H^*(G;R)).

nodes.name: tt-category
nodes.statement: In particular, the term \emph{tt-category} usually refers to a model of a tensor-triangulated category, and similarly for tt-functors.

nodes.name: Commutative ring spectrum
nodes.statement: By\emph{commutative ring spectrum} we mean an $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-ring spectrum, i.e., a coherently commutative ring spectrum in the symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category of spectra.

nodes.name: Discrete commutative algebra
nodes.statement: When we wish to emphasize that the ring in question is an ordinary ring, we will also add the adjective \emph{discrete}, as in \emph{discrete commutative algebra}.

nodes.name: Essentially small tt-category K
nodes.statement: Let $\cat K$ be an essentially small tensor-triangulated category.

nodes.name: Balmer spectrum
nodes.statement: Tensor-triangular geometry studies the structure of $\cat K$ by viewing it as a geometric object over an associated spectral topological space, its Balmer spectrum $\mathrm{Spc}(\cat K)$.

nodes.name: Balmer support
nodes.statement: The construction of the spectrum is accompanied by a support function which takes values in certain subsets of $\mathrm{Spc}(\cat K)$: \begin{equation} \xymatrix{\mathrm{supp}\colon \mathrm{Ob}\cat K \ar[r] & \{\text{closed subsets of } \mathrm{Spc}(\cat K)\}.} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The support function supp assigns to each object of K a closed subset of Spc(K).

nodes.name: Noetherian Balmer spectrum
nodes.statement: Assuming from now on that $\mathrm{Spc}(\cat K)$ is a Noetherian space, which covers all examples of tt-categories appearing in this paper, the Thomason subsets coincide with the specialization closed ones.

nodes.name: Balmer's classification of thick tensor ideals
nodes.statement: Balmer establishes a universal property for $\mathrm{supp}$ and proves that it classifies thick tensor ideals of $\cat K$. Explicitly, if $\cat K$ is rigid, the support function induces a bijection \[ \mathrm{supp}\colon\begin{Bmatrix} \text{Thick tensor ideals} \\ \text{of } \cat K \end{Bmatrix} \xymatrix@C=2pc{ \ar[r]^-{\sim} &} \begin{Bmatrix} \text{Specialization closed} \\ \text{subsets of } \mathrm{Spc}(\cat K) \end{Bmatrix}. \]
nodes.statement_short: For rigid K, Balmer support gives a bijection between thick tensor ideals and specialization closed subsets of Spc(K).
assumptions: if $\cat K$ is rigid
conclusions: the support function induces a bijection

nodes.name: Standing assumption for stratification
nodes.statement: In this subsection, we let $\cat T$ be a rigidly-compactly generated tt-category. In addition, we assume that the spectrum $\mathrm{Spc}(\cat T^c)$ is Noetherian.\footnote{This assumption is mostly for simplicity; the theory extends to weakly Noetherian spectra as well, see \cite{bhs1}.}

nodes.name: Balmer-Favi notion of support
nodes.statement: Under suitable point-set topological assumptions \cite{BalmerFavi11, bhs1} on $\mathrm{Spc}(\cat T^c)$, such as the one stipulated in \cref{conv:stratification}, the support function $\mathrm{supp}$ of \eqref{eq:Balmersupport} can be extended to all of $\cat T$: \begin{equation} \xymatrix{\mathrm{Supp}\colon \mathrm{Ob}\cat T \ar[r] & \mathbb{P}(\mathrm{Spc}(\cat T^c)) := \{\text{Subsets of } \mathrm{Spc}(\cat T^c)\};} \end{equation} we refer to this function as the \emph{Balmer--Favi notion of support}.
nodes.statement_short: Extension of Balmer support to all objects of T, valued in arbitrary subsets of Spc(T^c).

nodes.name: Balmer-Favi support map
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{\mathrm{Supp}\colon \mathrm{Ob}\cat T \ar[r] & \mathbb{P}(\mathrm{Spc}(\cat T^c)) := \{\text{Subsets of } \mathrm{Spc}(\cat T^c)\};}

nodes.name: Balmer-Favi support extends Balmer support
nodes.statement: In particular, it has the property that $\mathrm{Supp}(t) = \mathrm{supp}(t)$ for all $t\in \cat T^c$.

nodes.name: Support of a localizing ideal
nodes.statement: Moreover, setting $\mathrm{Supp}(\cat L) = \bigcup_{l \in \cat L}\mathrm{Supp}(l)$, we have $\mathrm{Supp}(\Loco{t}) = \mathrm{Supp}(t)$ for any $t\in \cat T$.

nodes.name: Collection of localizing ideals
nodes.statement: Therefore, the Balmer--Favi notion of support induces a function defined on all localizing ideals of $\cat T$, which we will usually denote by $\mathcal{L}\mathrm{oc}_{\otimes}(\cat T)$.

nodes.name: Stratified tt-category
nodes.statement: A compactly generated big tt-category $\cat T$ is said to be \emph{stratified} if the map \[ \mathrm{Supp}\colon\begin{Bmatrix} \text{Localizing tensor ideals of } \cat T \end{Bmatrix} \xymatrix@C=2pc{ \ar[r]^-{\sim} &} \begin{Bmatrix} \text{Subsets of } \mathrm{Spc}(\cat T^c) \end{Bmatrix} \] is a bijection.
nodes.statement_short: T is stratified if Balmer-Favi support is a bijection between localizing tensor ideals and subsets of Spc(T^c).
nodes.label: def:stratification

nodes.name: Set-generated localizing ideals
nodes.statement: More precisely, the stratification condition applies to the collection of all \emph{set-generated} localizing ideals of $\cat T$. In light of \cite[Prop.~3.5]{bhs1}, stratification in this sense implies that all localizing ideals of $\cat T$ are set-generated, which is why we leave the generated-by-a-set property implicit here.

nodes.name: Minimality criterion for stratification
nodes.statement: Under \cref{conv:stratification}, a tt-category $\cat T$ is stratified if and only if the following \emph{minimality condition} is satisfied for all $\cat P \in \mathrm{Spc}(\cat T^c)$: \begin{itemize} \item[] (Minimality) There are no nonzero proper localizing ideals contained in $\Gamma_{\cat P}\cat T = \SET{t \in \cat T}{\mathrm{Supp}(t) \subseteq \{\cat P\}}$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: T is stratified iff each local category Gamma_P T has no nonzero proper localizing ideals.
assumptions: Under \cref{conv:stratification}
conclusions: a tt-category $\cat T$ is stratified if and only if the following \emph{minimality condition} is satisfied for all $\cat P \in \mathrm{Spc}(\cat T^c)$

nodes.name: BIK local cohomology functors
nodes.statement: It depends on an auxiliary Noetherian graded commutative ring $R$ acting on $\cat T$, which is used to construct local cohomology functors $\Gamma_{\frak p}^{R \circlearrowright \cat T}$ for $\frak p \in \mathrm{Spec}^h(R)$.

nodes.name: BIK-notion of support
nodes.statement: The corresponding \emph{BIK-notion of support} is then defined, for any $t \in \cat T$, by \[ \mathrm{Supp}^{R \circlearrowright \cat T}(t) = \SET{\frak p \in \mathrm{Spec}^h(R)}{\Gamma_{\frak p}^{R \circlearrowright \cat T}(t) \neq 0}. \]

nodes.name: BIK-stratification
nodes.statement: Following \cite{BensonIyengarKrause11b}, we say that $\cat T$ is \emph{BIK-stratified} (with respect to the action of $R$ on $\cat T$) if $\Gamma_{\frak p}^{R \circlearrowright \cat T}\cat T$ is zero or minimal for any $\frak p \in \mathrm{Spec}^h(R)$.

nodes.name: BIK-stratification implies tt-stratification
nodes.statement: Suppose $\cat T$ is BIK-stratified by the action of a graded commutative Noetherian ring $R$. Then $\cat T$ is stratified (\cref{def:stratification}) and there exists a canonical homeomorphism $\mathrm{Supp}^{R \circlearrowright \cat T}(\cat T) \xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Spc}(\cat T^c)$. Under this homeomorphism, $\mathrm{Supp}^{R \circlearrowright \cat T}$ coincides with the Balmer--Favi notion of support $\mathrm{Supp}$. Moreover, if $R = [\mathbb{1},\mathbb{1}]^{\bullet}$ and $\cat T$ is stratified by the canonical action of $R$ on $\cat T$, then Balmer's comparison map \eqref{eq:Balmercomparisonmap}, \[ \xymatrix{\rho^{\bullet}\colon \mathrm{Spc}(\cat T^c) \ar[r]^-{\cong} & \mathrm{Spec}^h(R),} \] is a homeomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: BIK-stratification by a Noetherian ring implies tt-stratification, identifying BIK and Balmer-Favi support; for the endomorphism ring of the unit, Balmer's comparison map is a homeomorphism.

nodes.name: Descent for stratification
nodes.statement: Let $f^*\colon \cat S \to \cat T$ be a colimit preserving tt-functor between rigidly-compactly tt-categories with Noetherian spectra, and let $f_*$ be a right adjoint to $f_*$. Write $\varphi\colon \mathrm{Spc}(\cat T^c) \to \mathrm{Spc}(\cat S^c)$ for the map on spectra induced by $f^*$. Suppose that there exists a commutative algebra object $A \in \cat S$ and an equivalence of tt-categories $\cat T \simeq \mathrm{Mod}_{\cat S}(A)$ making the following diagram commute \[ \xymatrix{\cat S \ar[r]^-{f^*} \ar[dr]_-{-\otimes A} & \cat T \ar[d]^-{\sim} \\ & \mathrm{Mod}_{\cat S}(A).} \] In addition, assume one of the following conditions is satisfied: \begin{enumerate} \item[(1)] $f^*$ is a finite localization away from a Thomason subset $Y \subseteq \mathrm{Spc}(\cat S^c)$; \item[(2)] $A \in \cat S$ is compact and $\varphi$ is injective; \item[(3)] $A \in \cat S$ is compact and, as an algebra, faithful and separable of finite degree. \end{enumerate} If $\cat T$ is stratified, then the categories $\Gamma_{\frak p}\cat S$ are minimal for all $\frak p \in \mathrm{supp}(A)$.

nodes.name: Proof of descent for stratification
nodes.statement: Part (1) is an instance of Zariski descent for stratification, established in \cite[Cor.~5.3 and Rem.~5.4]{bhs1}, while Part (3) is proven in \cite[Thm.~2.14]{barthel_integral1}. Note that, for a finite localization away from $Y$ as in (1), $\mathrm{supp}(A)$ is the complement of $Y$, while in the case of (3), we have $\mathrm{supp}(A) = \mathrm{Spc}(\cat S^c)$. It remains to verify the claim in the case of (2). Let $A \in \mathrm{CAlg}(\cat S^c)$ and assume that the fiber of $\varphi$ is either empty or singleton. It follows from \cite[Thm.~1.7]{Balmer18} that $\mathrm{supp}(A) = \mathrm{im}(\varphi)$. Let $\frak p \in \mathrm{supp}(A)$ and write $\varphi^{-1}(\frak p) = \{\frak q\}$. By localizing away from $\langle \frak p \rangle$, we may assume that $\frak p$ is maximal in $\cat C$, see for example \cite[Ex.~5.7]{Sanders21pp}. The proofs of Lemmas 2.17, 2.18, and 2.19 of \cite{barthel_integral1} go through without the assumption that $A$ is a separable algebra of finite degree, using instead that $\varphi^{-1}(\frak p)$ is a singleton. We conclude that $\Gamma_{\frak p}\cat S$ is minimal if $\Gamma_{\frak q}\cat T$ is minimal, which holds by assumption. This finishes the proof.

nodes.name: Torus cochain conventions
nodes.statement: Throughout this subsection, $R$ denotes a commutative ring, not necessarily regular but later assumed to be Noetherian. Furthermore, $\mathbb{T} = (S^1)^{\times r}$ is a torus of rank $r$, which acts trivially on $R$. The resulting homotopy fixed point spectrum $R^{h\mathbb{T}}$ has the structure of a commutative ring spectrum which can be modelled by the commutative ring spectrum of cochains $C^*(B\mathbb{T},R)$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix a commutative ring R and a rank-r torus T acting trivially; R^{hT} is the commutative ring spectrum of cochains C^*(BT,R).

nodes.name: Formality of cochains on tori
nodes.statement: For any commutative ring $R$, the underlying $\mathbb{E}_1$-$R$-algebra of $R^{h\mathbb{T}}$ is formal. In algebraic terms, there is an equivalence \[ C^*(B\mathbb{T},R) \simeq \pi_{*}R^{h\mathbb{T}} \] of dg-algebras over $R$, where the graded cohomology ring $\pi_{-*}R^{h\mathbb{T}} \cong H^{*}(\mathbb{T};R)$ is equipped with the zero differential.

nodes.name: Proof of formality for tori
nodes.statement: The graded commutative cohomology ring of $R^{h\mathbb{T}}$ is isomorphic to a graded polynomial ring over $R$, \begin{equation} \pi_*R^{h\mathbb{T}} \cong R[x_1,\ldots,x_r], \end{equation} where each of the generators $x_i$ has (homological) degree $-2$. Represent these generators by maps $x_i\colon\Sigma^{-2}R \to R^{h\mathbb{T}}$ of $R$-module spectra. The induced map \[ \textstyle\bigoplus_{i=1}^r\Sigma^{-2}R \to R^{h\mathbb{T}} \] extends to a map of $\mathbb{E}_1$-$R$-algebras from the free $\mathbb{E}_1$-$R$-algebra on $\bigoplus_{i=1}^r\Sigma^{-2}R$: \[ \mathrm{Free}_{\mathbb{E}_1-R}(x_1,\ldots,x_r) \to R^{h\mathbb{T}}. \] By construction, this map induces an isomorphism on homotopy groups and thus exhibits the underlying $\mathbb{E}_1$-$R$-algebra of $R^{h\mathbb{T}}$ as formal. nodes.name: Proof of stratification for tori
nodes.statement: We employ the theory of BIK-stratification \cite{BensonIyengarKrause11b}, brielfy reviewed in \cref{ssec:recstratification} above, to prove this result; in light of \cref{thm:ttstratificationuniversality}, this suffices to show that $\mathrm{Mod}(R^{h\mathbb{T}})$ is also stratified in the tt-sense. Consider the tt-category $\mathrm{Mod}(R^{h\mathbb{T}})$ equipped with the canonical action by $\pi_*R^{h\mathbb{T}}$. As an $\mathbb{E}_1$-algebra, $\pi_*R^{h\mathbb{T}}$ is formal by \cref{lem:formality}; furthermore, it is Noetherian because $R$ is Noetherian. The equivalence of $\mathbb{E}_1$-algebras $R^{h\mathbb{T}} \simeq \pi_*R^{h\mathbb{T}}$ induces an equivalence of stable $\infty$-categories \[ \mathrm{Mod}(R^{h\mathbb{T}}) \simeq \mathrm{Mod}(\pi_*R^{h\mathbb{T}}). \] Via the transfer principle of \cite[Cor.~8.4]{BensonIyengarKrause11b}, it suffices to show that $\mathrm{Mod}(\pi_*R^{h\mathbb{T}})$ is stratified by the induced action of $\pi_*R^{h\mathbb{T}}$. Since $\pi_*R^{h\mathbb{T}}$ is a commutative dg-algebra which is formal as a dg-algebra, \cite[Thm.~8.1]{BensonIyengarKrause11b} applies to give the desired stratification result. It therefore remains to determine the Balmer spectrum of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^{h\mathbb{T}})$. To this end, observe that the residue fields $\kappa(\frak p)$ of $\pi_*R^{h\mathbb{T}}$ are non-trivial for all $\frak p \in \mathrm{Spec}^h(\pi_*R^{h\mathbb{T}})$, hence the BIK-support of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^{h\mathbb{T}})$ is all of $\mathrm{Spec}^h(\pi_*R^{h\mathbb{T}})$. The first isomorphism of \eqref{eq:spctorus} thus follows from \cref{thm:ttstratificationuniversality}, while the second is a consequence of \eqref{eq:cohomologytorus}.

nodes.name: Field and elementary abelian group conventions
nodes.statement: In this section, we will work over a fixed field $k$ and consider discrete commutative algebras $A$ over $k$. If the characteristic of $k$ is different from $p$, the results of this subsection hold trivially, so we may tacitly assume $\mathrm{char}(k) = p$.

nodes.name: Proof of Galois extension lemma
nodes.statement: In \cite[Prop.~3.9]{mathew_torus} (see also \cite[\S9]{mathew_galois}), Mathew establishes this result for $A = k$. The general case follows from this by base-change. By \cref{lem:groupcohomologybasechange} applied twice, the left inner square and outer rectangle are pushout squares in the category of commutative $k$-algebras. Therefore, the right inner square is a pushout as well. It follows from base-change for faithful Galois extensions, proven by Rognes in \cite[Lem.~7.1.1]{Rognes08}, that $A^{h\mathbb{T}} \to A^{hE}$ is a faithful Galois extension with Galois group $\mathbb{T}$, as desired.

nodes.name: Borel equivariant ring spectrum
nodes.statement: Let $\mathrm{Sp}_G$ be the symmetric monoidal stable $\infty$-category of genuine equivariant $G$-spectra for $G$ a finite group, see for example \cite[Part 2]{MathewNaumannNoel17} or the classical \cite{LewisMaySteinbergerMcClure86}. Denote the inflation functor by $\mathrm{infl}\colon \mathrm{Sp} \to \mathrm{Sp}_G$; this is the tt-functor which sends a spectrum $M$ to a $G$-spectrum with trivial $G$-action. If $R$ is a commutative ring spectrum, we write $\underline{R}_G = F(EG_+,\mathrm{infl} R) \in \mathrm{Sp}_G$ for the $G$-Borel equivariant commutative ring spectrum associated to $R$.

nodes.name: Proof via derived Morita theory
nodes.statement: The result follows from derived Morita theory proven by Schwede and Shipley~\cite{SS03} and Lurie~\cite[Thm.~7.1.2.1]{HALurie}, as soon as we have verified the following two claims: \begin{enumerate} \item $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_P}(\underline{A}_P)$ is compactly generated by its unit $\underline{A}_P$; \item the derived endomorphisms of $\underline{A}_P$ are equivalent to $A^{hP}$, as commutative ring spectra. \end{enumerate} For the first claim, note that the unit homomorphism $\eta\colon k \to A$ induces a tt-functor \[ \xymatrix{\eta^*\colon \mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_P}(\underline{k}_P) \ar[r] & \mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_P}(\underline{A}_P),} \] whose forgetful right adjoint is conservative. In particular, $\eta^*$ preserves compact generators. Since $P$ is a finite $p$-group, $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_P}(\underline{k}_P) \simeq \mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}}(k^{tP})$ is compactly generated by its unit. Therefore, the same is true for $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_P}(\underline{A}_P)$. In order to see (2), we compute \[ \mathrm{End}_{\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_P}(\underline{A}_P)}(\underline{A}_P) \simeq \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{Sp}_P}(S_P^0,\underline{A}_P) \simeq \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{Sp}_P}(EP_+,\mathrm{infl} A) \simeq A^{hP}. \] As in \cite[\S2.2]{mathew_torus}, this equivalence is compatible with the commutative ring spectra structures on both sides, which implies the claim.

nodes.name: Proof of injectivity via tori
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbb{T} = (S^{1})^{\times r}$ be a torus of rank $r$ and view $E \subset \mathbb{T}$ via the embedding of the $p$-th roots of unity. By naturality, the reduction map $q\colon R\to R/p$ fits into a commutative square of graded commutative cohomology rings: \begin{equation} \vcenter{ \xymatrix{H^*(E;R) \ar[d] & H^*(\mathbb{T};R) \ar[l] \ar[d] \\ H^*(E;R/p) & H^*(\mathbb{T};R/p). \ar[l] } } \end{equation} First, we claim that the bottom horizontal map is an $F$-isomorphism. Indeed, the proof of \cref{lem:groupcohomologybasechange} shows that $H^*(\mathbb{T};R/p) \to H^*(E;R/p)$ identifies with \[ H^*(\mathbb{T};\mathbb{F}_p) \otimes_{\mathbb{F}_p} R/p \to H^*(E;\mathbb{F}_p) \otimes_{\mathbb{F}_p} R/p, \] base-changed from the $F$-isomorphism $H^*(\mathbb{T};\mathbb{F}_p) \to H^*(E;\mathbb{F}_p)$. This implies the claim. Second, the right vertical map in \eqref{eq:lem:injectivity1} may be identified with the projection \[ R[y_1,\ldots,y_r] \to R/p[y_1,\ldots,y_r] \] with $|y_i| = -2$ for all $i$. Applying homogeneous Zariski spectra to the square \eqref{eq:lem:injectivity1} thus yields a commutative diagam \begin{equation} \xymatrix{\mathrm{Spec}^h(H^*(E;R)) \ar[r] & \mathrm{Spec}^h(H^*(\mathbb{T};R)) \\ \mathrm{Spec}^h(H^*(E;R/p)) \ar[r]_-{\cong} \ar[u]^-{\mathrm{Spec}^h(H^*(q))} & \mathrm{Spec}^h(H^*(\mathbb{T};R/p)), \ar@{^{(}->}[u]} \end{equation} in which the composite factoring through the right bottom term is injective. It follows that $\mathrm{Spec}^h(H^*(q))$ is injective as well.\footnote{Alternatively, this statement can also be verified by direct computation.} Let $q^*\colon \mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}^c(\underline{R}_E) \to \mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}^c(\underline{R/p}_E)$ denote base-change along $q$. Naturality of Balmer's comparison map \eqref{eq:Balmercomparisonmap} then provides a commutative square of spectra \[ \xymatrixcolsep{5pc}{ \xymatrix{\mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}^c(\underline{R/p}_E)) \ar[r]^-{\mathrm{Spc}(q^*)} \ar[d]_{\rho^{\bullet}}^{\cong} & \mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}^c(\underline{R}_E)) \ar[d]_{\cong}^{\rho^{\bullet}} \\ \mathrm{Spec}^h(H^*(E;R/p)) \ar@{^{(}->}[r]_{\mathrm{Spec}^h(H^*(q))} & \mathrm{Spec}^h(H^*(E;R)).}} \] Note that the vertical comparison maps are homeomorphisms by Lau's theorem and \cref{thm:elabstratificationmodp}, respectively. It follows that $\mathrm{Spc}(q^*)$ is injective, as desired.

nodes.name: Proof by modular lifting and descent
nodes.statement: Any regular commutative ring decomposes as a finite product of regular integral domains. Since the formation of the categories $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_G}(\underline{R}_G)$ commutes with finite products, we can reduce to $R$ itself being a regular domain. If $p$ is zero in $R$, then the result is a special case of \cref{prop:elabeqstratificationcharp}, so it remains to consider the case that $p \in R$ is regular. In order to prepare for the proof, we begin with the construction of two tt-functors, $q^*$ and $f^*$, with the following two properties: \begin{enumerate} \item on Balmer spectra, the functors $q^*$ and $f^*$ induce a jointly bijective map; \item the target categories of $q^*$ and $f^*$ are stratified. \end{enumerate} We will then argue by descent, appealing to the techniques from \cref{ssec:ttascentanddescent}. The quotient map $R \to R/p$ induces a morphism $q\colon \underline{R}_E \to \underline{R/p}_E$ of commutative $E$-equivariant ring spectra, and hence a colimit preserving tt-functor \[ \xymatrix{q^*\colon\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}(\underline{R}_E) \ar[r] & \mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}(\underline{R/p}_E).} \] Its forgetful right adjoint $q_*$ is conservative and preserves compact objects: Indeed, $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}(\underline{R/p}_E)$ is monogenic by \cref{prop:monogenicborel} and $\underline{R/p}_E \simeq \mathrm{cof}(\underline{R}_E \xrightarrow{p} \underline{R}_E)$, viewed as an $\underline{R}_E$-module, is compact. This suffices to apply \cite[Thm.~1.7]{Balmer18}, which shows that \begin{equation} \mathrm{supp}(\underline{R/p}_E) = \mathrm{im}(\varphi); \end{equation} here, $\varphi\colon \mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}^c(\underline{R/p}_E)) \to \mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}^c(\underline{R}_E))$ is the map on spectra induced by $q^*$. By \cref{lem:injectivity}, $\varphi = \mathrm{Spc}(q^*)$ is injective. Consider the finite (Verdier) localization of $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}(\underline{R}_E)$ away from the localizing ideal $\Loco{\underline{R/p}_E}$: \[ \xymatrix{f^*\colon \mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}(\underline{R}_E) \ar[r] & \mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}(\underline{R[1/p]}_E).} \] The category of local objects is as stated, because localizing away from the cofiber of multiplication by $p$ has the effect of inverting $p$, which in turn can be performed on the level of the unit. By virtue of \cref{prop:monogenicborel} and the fact that the group cohomology ring $\pi_*R^{hE} \cong H^*(E;R)$ is $p^{\mathrm{rank}_p(E)}$-torsion in all non-zero degrees, we can identify the target of $f^*$ further as \[ \mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}(\underline{R[1/p]}_E) \simeq \mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}}((R[1/p])^{hE}) \simeq \mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}}(R[1/p]). \] The induced injective map $\psi\colon \mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}}^c(R[1/p])) \to \mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}^c(\underline{R}_E))$ on spectra exhibits the domain as the quasi-compact open subset complementing $\mathrm{supp}(\underline{R/p}_E)$. Combined with \eqref{eq:suppofRmodp} this shows that $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are jointly surjective, thereby establishing Property (a) above. Property (b) holds as well, using \cref{prop:elabeqstratificationcharp} and Neeman's stratification theorem for derived categories of Noetherian commutative rings, \cite[Thm.~2.8]{Neeman92a}. After this preparation, we can now descend stratification along $f^*$ and $q^*$. To this end, first consider a local category $\Gamma_{\frak p}\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}(\underline{R}_E)$ for a prime tt-ideal $\frak p \in \mathrm{im}(\psi) \subseteq \mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}^c(\underline{R}_E))$. Since $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}}(R[1/p])$ is stratified, $\Gamma_{\frak p}\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}(\underline{R}_E)$ is minimal by Zariski descent \cref{prop:ttdescent}(1). If $\frak p \in \mathrm{im}(\varphi)$ instead, we deduce minimality of $\Gamma_{\frak p}\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}(\underline{R}_E)$ via \'etale descent along $f^*$, using \cref{prop:ttdescent}(2). Finally, it remains to observe that $\mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{E}}^c(\underline{R}_E))$ is Noetherian and homeo-morphic to $\mathrm{Spec}^h(\pi_*R^{hE})$, thanks to Lau's theorem \cite{lau_spcdmstacks}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a regular domain; descend stratification jointly along reduction mod p and inverting p. The key step: reduction mod p is injective on spectra, so etale descent applies.

nodes.statement: We offer some comments on the derived category of representations considered in this paper. Since it is rigidly-compactly generated, $\mathrm{Rep}(G,R)$ is determined as a symmetric monoidal category by its full subcategory of compact objects $\mathrm{rep}(G,R) = \mathrm{Fun}(BG,\mathrm{Perf}(R))$. Its homotopy category $\mathrm{Ho}(\mathrm{rep}(G,R))$ can be identified with the following categories: \begin{enumerate} \item The bounded derived category of modules over $R[G]$ whose underlying complex of $R$-modules is perfect. \item The category of perfect complexes over the Deligne--Mumford quotient stack $[\mathrm{Spec}(R)/G]$, when $R$ is a regular commutative ring equipped with trivial $G$-action. \end{enumerate} Furthermore, $\mathrm{Rep}(G,R)$ admits a canonical localization functor to the unbounded derived category $D(R[G])$ whose kernel is by definition our version of the stable module category $\mathrm{StMod}(G,R)$ with coefficients in a general commutative ring $R$. In fact, this localization sequence promotes to a recollement familiar from Rickard's presentation of the stable module category with field coefficients. The stable module category $\mathrm{StMod}(G,R)$ also admits an algebraic model; we refer to \cite[Sec.~3.3]{barthel_integral1} for the details. In short, let $\mathrm{Lat}(G,R)$ be the category of $R$-linear $G$-representations with underlying projective $R$-module. The category of such representations inherits a Frobenius exact structure from the abelian category $\mathrm{Mod}(R[G])$ in which it is embedded. Likewise, the $R$-linear tensor product on $\mathrm{Mod}(R[G])$ restricts to a symmetric monoidal structure on $\mathrm{Lat}(G,R)$. The homotopy category of the associated Quillen exact model structure is then canonically equivalent to the homotopy category of the $\infty$-category $\mathrm{StMod}(G,R)$ as tt-categories.
nodes.statement_short: Algebraic models of rep(G,R), Rep(G,R) and the stable module category StMod(G,R), including the lattice category Lat(G,R).
nodes.label: rem:incarnations

nodes.name: Equivariant-to-representation translation
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a finite group and $R$ a regular commutative ring. There is a commutative diagram of colimit preserving tt-functors \begin{equation} \vcenter{ \xymatrix{\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_G}(\underline{R}_G) \ar[r]^-{\sim} \ar[d]_{\theta^*} & \mathrm{Rep}(G,R) \ar[d]^{\theta^*} \\ \mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_G}(\underline{R}_G \otimes \widetilde{EG}) \ar[r]_-{\sim} & \mathrm{StMod}(G,R)} } \end{equation} in which the vertical maps are finite localizations away from $\Loco{\underline{R}_G\otimes G_+}$ and $\Loco{R[G]}$, respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Borel-equivariant R-modules are equivalent to Rep(G,R), compatibly with the localizations to the Tate side and StMod(G,R).
assumptions: Let $G$ be a finite group and $R$ a regular commutative ring.
conclusions: There is a commutative diagram of colimit preserving tt-functors
nodes.label: prop:eqreptranslation

nodes.name: Generation by permutation modules
nodes.statement: The top equivalence in Diagram \eqref{eq:equivtorep} is a homotopical manifestation of the generation by permutation modules principle proven by Rouquier~\cite{Rouquier_letter}, Mathew~\cite[App.~A]{treumannmathew_reps}, and Balmer--Gallauer~\cite{balmergallauer_permmodulesres}. More generally, for coefficients in any commutative ring spectrum $S$, there is a colimit preserving tt-functor \[ \xymatrix{\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_G}(\underline{S}_G) \ar[r] & \mathrm{Rep}(G,S)} \] which is fully faithful. The question of when this functor is also essentially surjective will be studied further in joint work in progress with Gallauer.

nodes.name: Stratification of Rep(G,R) for regular coefficients
nodes.statement: Suppose $G$ is a finite group and $R$ is a regular commutative ring, then $\mathrm{Rep}(G,R)$ is stratified over $\mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{rep}(G,R)) \cong \mathrm{Spec}^h(H^*(G;R))$.
also_stated_at: The category $\mathrm{Rep}(G,R)$ is stratified for any finite group $G$ and any regular commutative ring $R$.
nodes.statement_short: For finite G and regular R, the derived representation category Rep(G,R) is stratified over Spec^h(H^*(G;R)).
assumptions: Suppose $G$ is a finite group and $R$ is a regular commutative ring
conclusions: then $\mathrm{Rep}(G,R)$ is stratified over $\mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{rep}(G,R)) \cong \mathrm{Spec}^h(H^*(G;R))$.

nodes.name: Proof of stratification of Rep(G,R)
nodes.statement: If $G = E$ is an elementary abelian $p$-group for some prime $p$, the category $\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sp}_E}(\underline{R}_E)$ is stratified by \cref{thm:elabeqstratification}. Combined with \cref{prop:eqreptranslation}, this implies the result for $\mathrm{Rep}(E,R)$. The case of a general finite group then follows from this via finite \'etale descent (\cref{prop:ttdescent}(3)), as shown in \cite[Thm.~4.18(1)]{barthel_integral1}. Finally, the identification of the spectrum $\mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{rep}(G,R))$ is the content of Lau's theorem \cite{lau_spcdmstacks}.
nodes.statement_short: Elementary abelian case from the equivariant theorem and translation; general groups by finite etale descent; spectrum by Lau's theorem.

nodes.name: Classification, telescope conjecture and tensor product formula for Rep(G,R)
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $R$ be a regular commutative ring. The universal support function composed with Balmer's comparison map induces a bijection \[ \mathrm{Supp}\colon\begin{Bmatrix} \text{Localizing tensor ideals} \\ \text{of } \cat \mathrm{Rep}(G,R) \end{Bmatrix} \xymatrix@C=2pc{ \ar[r]^-{\sim} &} \begin{Bmatrix} \text{Subsets of} \\ \mathrm{Spec}^h(H^*(G;R)) \end{Bmatrix}. \] Moreover, the telecope conjecture holds in $\mathrm{Rep}(G,R)$, so that we obtain bijections \[ \begin{Bmatrix} \text{Smashing ideals} \\ \text{of } \cat \mathrm{Rep}(G,R) \end{Bmatrix} \simeq \begin{Bmatrix} \text{Thick tensor ideals} \\ \text{of } \cat \mathrm{rep}(G,R) \end{Bmatrix} \simeq \begin{Bmatrix} \text{Specialization closed} \\ \text{subsets of } \mathrm{Spec}^h(H^*(G;R)) \end{Bmatrix}, \] and support satisfies the tensor product formula for any $M,N \in \mathrm{Rep}(G,R)$: \[ \mathrm{Supp}(M \otimes N) = \mathrm{Supp}(M) \cap \mathrm{Supp}(N). \]
also_stated_at: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $R$ be a regular commutative ring. The telescope conjecture holds in $\mathrm{Rep}(G,R)$ and cohomological support satisfies the tensor product formula.

nodes.name: Stratification of StMod(G,R)
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a regular ring and $G$ a finite group. The stable module category $\mathrm{StMod}(G,R)$ is stratified over \[ \mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{StMod}^c(G,R)) \cong \mathrm{Proj}(H^*(G;R)). \] In particular, the telescope conjecture and the tensor product formula for cohomological support hold in $\mathrm{StMod}(G,R)$.

nodes.name: Proof of stratification of StMod(G,R)
nodes.statement: Since stratification ascends along finite localizations (\cite[Cor.~5.5]{bhs1}), we see that $\mathrm{StMod}(G,R)$ is stratified by \cref{prop:eqreptranslation} and \cref{thm:repstratification}. Moreover, \cite[Cor.~3.32]{barthel_integral1} provides a natural homeomorphism \[ \mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{StMod}^c(G,R)) \cong \mathrm{Proj}(H^*(G;R)), \] thus finishing the proof.
